chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwān, from 'Amr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn 'Alī, from his fathers, from 'Alī (peace be upon him) that he said:
"A single suckling is like a hundred sucklings; it is permissible for him [to marry her] forever."

Therefore, this report is also to be understood in light of the two interpretations we previously mentioned regarding the first report. Its chain of narration testifies to this, because the narrators of this report are from the people of the Sunnah (general) and the Zaydis, and no one else has narrated it from them. And since its path is not strong, it is not obligatory to act upon it.

key_terms.رِجَالُ الْعَامَّةِ: Narrators from the general Sunni tradition
key_terms.لَا يَجِبُ الْعَمَلُ بِهِ: It is not obligatory to act upon it

ai.seo_question: Does a single breastfeeding create a permanent marriage prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* reinforces the principle that a single suckling establishes a permanent mahram relationship, equating one instance to a hundred. However, the scholar highlights its specific chain of narration (isnad) through the Zaydis and Sunnis, noting that while it is not obligatory to act upon it exclusively, it remains valid under the broader interpretive frameworks previously discussed in the chapter.
